newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian PM vows justice reform in child sex case.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM vows justice reform in child sex case.

text.p: The Belgian government vowed on Tuesday to reform the country's police and justice systems in a bid to restore public confidence after a scandal of child abduction, sexual abuse and murder gripped the country.
"The confidence of our citizens in our institutions has been shaken," Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene told the opening session of the new parliamentary year.
"During the coming months the government will take important decisions on this matter," he added. "It is truly a hurricane that has battered our country these past weeks."

Dehaene said these key decisions would cover the appointment of public prosecutors, the division of responsibilities between different police forces, relations between the police and the judiciary and the enforcement of penalties.

The unmasking of the child abduction, sexual abuse and murder ring allegedly led by convicted rapist Marc Dutroux has left Belgium in a state of shock and prompted hitherto unasked questions about the moral and political health of the country.
Four young girls have been found dead since mid-August -- two at least starved to death. Two others have been rescued.
Police have also unearthed the body of a former accomplice whom Dutroux admits killing, and are actively searching for at least seven other missing children.
The case has revealed a catalogue of bungling, incompetence and rivalry between different police forces and the judiciary, and prompted allegations of possible police complicity.
Dehaene promised that nothing would be allowed to hamper either the investigations into the crimes or the new investigations into the past inquiries. Heads would roll if necessary, he added.
